A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CQN-AS research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B support comparison despite the changed title and layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original CQN-AS experiments on BiGym, HumanoidBench, and RLBench, together with ablations and torque-control failure analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark experiments and ablations, including additional demonstration-smoothing, actor-critic overestimation, and hyperparameter analyses.

M1.justification: The coarse-to-fine critic, GRU architecture, temporal ensemble, and replay procedure are retained. However, Table 4 changes HumanoidBench's dueling-network setting from False to True while v2 Appendix A still says it is disabled, leaving the actual component change unresolved. The expanded N-step objective alone does not establish a new procedure: v1 already specifies N=3 for HumanoidBench.

E1.justification: Both retain 25 BiGym tasks, eight HumanoidBench tasks, 20 RLBench tasks, and the Walker Run/Cheetah Run torque-control analyses. Appendix task lists are unchanged. New diagnostics vary action processing or algorithm settings within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: v1 Figure 5 compares CQN-AS with CQN, SAC, DreamerV3, and TD-MPC2; v2 Figure 6 retains only CQN and SAC, eliminating the model-based comparison class across HumanoidBench. Appendix A still names the removed methods but supplies no corresponding v2 results. The manipulation comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 3 increases BiGym training and demonstration batch sizes from 128 each to 256 each. Appendix A changes HumanoidBench training from seven to ten million steps, and Table 4 shortens its target-update interval from 1000 to 100. Added experiments introduce smoothing procedures, SAC/TD3 action-sequence configurations, and N-step and ensemble-weight sweeps. These are reported setting changes, without establishing which earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 Figures 1–2 add trajectory visualizations, demonstration-smoothing tests, and action-sequence overestimation diagnostics for SAC/TD3. Figure 8c tests N-step returns of 1, 4, and 16; Figure 8e tests temporal-ensemble weights. The earlier sequence-length, RL-objective, ensemble-removal, and torque-control analyses remain.

E5.justification: Reported aggregation increases from four to eight runs for BiGym and for CQN-AS/CQN on HumanoidBench. RLBench and ablations remain at four runs, and the borrowed SAC results remain at three. Mean-and-confidence-interval reporting is retained without a new statistical estimation method.

E6.justification: BiGym and HumanoidBench learning curves are revised under changed settings and run counts, so they do not establish same-setting performance gains or losses. New Figure 1 reports approximately 100% replay success for raw demonstrations versus 78% for average smoothing and 63% for median/exponential smoothing. Figures 2 and 8 add overestimation and sensitivity findings, while model-based benchmark results are removed.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 1 replaces the single reward in v1 Equation 4 with an N-reward sum, revising the mathematical objective. However, v2 Appendix B.2 retains the earlier one-step expression. The multidimensional formulation is otherwise substantially unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains learning action-sequence Q-values for data-efficient robotic control. v2's introduction additionally claims that the critic-only construction obtains action-sequence benefits while avoiding actor-critic value overestimation, extending the earlier emphasis on learning from noisy trajectories.

C2.justification: v2 develops a credit-assignment explanation, argues that smoothing sacrifices action precision, and attributes actor-critic failure to exploiting approximation errors in enlarged action spaces. It adds explanations concerning N-step return variance and ensemble-weight/reactivity trade-offs. Existing delicate-object and torque-control limitations remain, while the interpretation of competitiveness with model-based methods is removed.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses HumanoidBench's update-to-data ratio of 0.5 and revises hardware and timing information, specifying A5000 GPUs for BiGym/HumanoidBench. It removes the precise BiGym demonstration commit/date and the explicit promise to release the full code. Most implementation and access information remains; the PDFs do not establish an actual change in code availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds Minsky (1961) and Fujimoto et al. (2018) for the revised motivation, plus Doshi et al. (2024) and Kim et al. (2024) for future vision-language-action work. References including RT-1, RT-2, and Metz et al. (2017) are removed. The dedicated related-work discussion and principal positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: The title changes, and the abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around credit assignment, actor-critic failure, and the rationale for CQN-AS. Background and method sections are renamed and reworded, experimental setup prose is condensed, and explanatory paragraphs are reorganized. This substantially changes the narrative beyond adding scientific content.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column layout. v1's summary plot is removed; v2 adds diagnostic Figures 1–2, redraws the inference/architecture and task-example illustrations, and expands the ablation display from four to six panel groups. Benchmark plots and appendix tables are also resized or rearranged.

improvement.justification: The added sensitivity studies test previously underexamined design choices, increased reported replication strengthens experimental support, and the redrawn inference diagram improves explanation. These provide a modest overall gain. Removing model-based comparisons reduces context, while the contradictory dueling-network setting and unreconciled objective formulations limit the improvement in clarity and reproducibility.
